_why: The exact bodies web/src/components/DeviceForm.tsx sends to POST /devices, held in one
file so the two planes cannot drift apart. The web suite asserts the form emits these;
the BFF suite relays these through ContractGateway, which enforces the gateway's real
refusals. Neither suite alone can prove the pair: the browser one has no gateway rules
and the Python one has no form. LR-48 lived in exactly that gap for three weeks -- a
registration body that no gateway would ever accept, green in both suites, because each
was asserted against its own double.
A case removed from here must be removed from both suites, which is the point: deleting
coverage has to be deliberate rather than a side effect of editing one language.

Update bodies live here too, under `update_cases`: the console composes a PUT as well, and the gateway refuses `expected_tls_spki_sha256` there while honouring `fingerprint_policy` -- opposite answers to two fields that sit side by side in the form.

openapi-with-api-key._note: The ordinary registration. Carries no upstream_transport: the gateway refuses that key on an openapi device on PRESENCE, so even the correct value is a 400.

mcp-server._note: spec_url is an explicit null rather than absent. On a PUT the gateway reads data.get('spec_url', existing.spec_url), so omitting it preserves a stored OpenAPI document into a combination it then refuses.

tighten-the-policy._note: Policy is settable on an update. The pin is NOT, and must never appear in a PUT body.

clear-the-policy._note: An explicit null clears the override and inherits the fleet default. Absent would leave the stored value alone, so the two cannot be collapsed.

an-ordinary-edit._note: Says nothing about the policy, and nothing about the pin.
